learning_outcomes.text: Understand the description and classifications of crystals through polyhedral representations of inorganic crystal structures.
Understand band structure: Electronic structure derived from crystal structure, and structure-property relations.
Understand non-stoichiometry and defects in crystals: Manipulation and control of the physical properties of solids.
Understand synthetic methods and characterization in inorganic solids: Crystal Growth of single-crystals, polycrystalline and amorphous solids.
Understand the application of inorganic compounds in technology.
Relate the structure of matter with the physical properties of solids.
Relate the structure of matter with technological applications of advanced materials.
Perform practical exercises on crystal structure determination from X-ray diffraction data.
Develop skill in writing scientific manuscripts in English.
Develop skill in public presentation of a scientific topic.

syllabus_topics: Structure types of Solids: Metals and Nonmetals
Structure types of Solids: Binary compounds (ΑΒ, ΑΒ2, ΑΒ3, Α2Β3, ΑxBy)
Structure types of Solids: Ternary compounds (ΑΒΧ2, ΑΒΧ3, ΑΒ3, ΑΒ2Χ4, Α2ΒΧ4, ΑB2Χ2)
Structure types of Solids: Intermetallics and Zintl Phases
Structure types of Solids: Modular compounds (Polytypes, Homologous series and misfit layered compounds)
Band structure (based on R. Hoffmann review): Constructing “Spaghetti” diagrams starting from molecular orbitals
Band structure (based on R. Hoffmann review): Electronic instability (Peierls distortion, Jahn-Teller effect)
Band structure (based on R. Hoffmann review): Density of states, band folding, direct and indirect bandgap
Band structure (based on R. Hoffmann review): Quantum confinement (Low-dimensional materials, Quantum wells, Quantum wires, Quantum dots)
Non-Stoichiometry and Defects in Crystals: Nonstoichiometry and diffusion, thermal quenching, sintering, and annealing
Non-Stoichiometry and Defects in Crystals: Phase diagrams, eutectics, spinodal decomposition and solid solutions
Non-Stoichiometry and Defects in Crystals: Phase transitions in inorganic solids, crystals and amorphous solids
Synthesis methods: Solid-state synthesis, wet synthesis, solvothermal synthesis
Synthesis methods: Crystal Growth (Growth from melts, solutions and vapor transport)
Synthesis methods: Structural characterization (Structure determination from single-crystals and crystalline powders, Characterization of amorphous solids using Pair Distribution Functions (PDF))
Applications of Inorganic Compounds in Modern Era Technology: Inorganic Semiconductors in Optoelectronics (Photodiodes in Photovoltaics, Detectors and LED’s)
Applications of Inorganic Compounds in Modern Era Technology: Porous Materials (Gas Separation and Catalysis)
Applications of Inorganic Compounds in Modern Era Technology: Hydrogen Technology (Production, Storage and Reactivity)
Applications of Inorganic Compounds in Modern Era Technology: Energy Storage (Solid State Batteries)
teaching_methods: Use of interactive online databases (ionic radii, physical properties of semiconductors, ICSD, CSD)
Use of visualization and analysis software of the crystal structure

assessment_methods.method: Writing of a scientific manuscript in English

assessment_rules: Successful completion of the course involves the writing of a scientific manuscript in English (40%) and its oral presentation in the class (40%). The remaining 20% is evaluated based on class participation and understanding throughout the course. The topic will be chosen by the student after consultation with the instructor.
